text.p: Terry Norris stopped a very tough Alex Rios to retain his two 154-pound (69.8 kg) titles when the referee stopped their fight at two minutes, eight seconds of the fifth round on Saturday.
Norris pounded Rios almost at will throughout the fight, landing punishing left-right hooks followed by hard combinations. But Rios kept coming back for more.
Norris, who retired Sugar Ray Leonard with a 12-round decision in 1991, kept his World Boxing Council (WBC) and International Boxing Federation (IBF) titles.

At one point in the second round Norris was teeing off on Rios with target practice. Rios, on the ropes, appeared only a punch or two away from being knocked out but came back to land punches of his own, and at the bell he pounded his chest for the crowd, proud to have survived the Norris onslaught.

Norris, 30, dropped Rios to one knee for a nanosecond, so fast that referee Mills Lane did not appear to have seen it. Rios came back yet again and the two Americans were trading punches when the bell rang, although Rios did not have nearly the power in his blows that Norris had.
Rios folded to the canvas again in the fourth round on a delayed rection to a left to the side of his head. He came back again after an eight count.
Norris staggered the 26-year-old Rios with a right to the head in the fifth round and followed with combinations to the head that brought Lane in to stop the scheduled 12-round bout.
The crowd of about 9,000 booed the stoppage, apparently believing Rios could have survived as he had earlier. Rios threw his hands up in the air, his face contorted in disbelief.
Norris, who first won the WBC title by knocking out John Mugabi in the first round in 1990, is now 44-6. Rios is 18-3.
Norris lost the WBC title when Simon Brown knocked him out in the fourth round in December 1993. He won it back from Brown on a 12-round decision three months later.
But Norris lost it again to Luis Santana in November 1994 on a disqualification after a late blow, and in a rematch the next April lost again on disqualification.
In August of 1995, in their third fight, Norris stopped Santana in the second round.
Norris won the IBF title in December 1995 on a 12-round decision over Paul Vaden.
